# Data Model: SEO Metadata Correctness + Article Slug-Pairing Fix + OG Images

**No database schema changes.** No new table, column, index, or constraint. No migration is generated by this feature (FR-013, AC-8). Every shape below is either an existing database column newly *selected* by a read that didn't select it before, or an in-memory TypeScript type used to pass data between a page's `generateMetadata`/page body and `lib/metadata.ts` / the client language switcher.

## Existing entities touched (read-only)

### Article (`articles` table, `lib/db/schema.ts:56-91` — unchanged)

No columns added or altered. This feature adds a **read** of the already-existing `translation_group_id` column in one place it wasn't previously read publicly:

| Field | Existing? | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `translation_group_id` (uuid) | Yes — already exists, already indexed, already used by admin reads | Newly included in the public `Article` TypeScript type (`lib/db/articles.ts:15-25`) and in `getArticleBySlug`'s select list (`lib/db/articles.ts:53-73`), so the public article-detail page can resolve its own group id without a second query. |
| `language`, `slug`, `published` | Yes | Read exactly as today by the new `getPublishedCounterpartSlug` function — no change to these columns' definitions. |

### Project (`projects` table — unchanged)

No columns added or altered, no new reads beyond what already exists (`getPortfolioDetailBySlug`, `getPortfolioSlugs`). Projects have no `published`/draft column; "not found" is the only non-indexable state a project detail page can be in (confirmed in `lib/db/schema.ts:21-39` and the source spec's assumptions).

## New/changed in-memory types (application code, not the database)

### `Article` (public type, `lib/db/articles.ts`)

Gains one field:

```ts
export type Article = {
  slug: string;
  title: string;
  excerpt: string;
  coverImage: string;
  body: string;
  published: boolean;
  publishedAt: Date | null;
  relatedProjectId: number | null;
  relatedSolution: string | null;
  translationGroupId: string; // new
};
```

### `PageMetadataInput` (`lib/metadata.ts`)

Gains two optional fields (see `research.md` §2 for the exact semantics):

```ts
export type PageMetadataInput = {
  path: string;
  language: Language;
  title: string;
  description: string;
  languageAlternates?: { en: string | null; ar: string | null }; // new — paths, not URLs
  imageUrl?: string; // new — relative path, e.g. "/api/image/42"
};
```

### Language-alternate override (new client-side context state, `lib/language-alternate-context.tsx`)

Not persisted anywhere — lives only in a client React Context for the lifetime of a single page render:

```ts
type LanguageAlternateOverride = string | null | undefined;
// undefined = no override published (naive switcher behavior, all non-article pages)
// string    = resolved counterpart path (article page, counterpart exists)
// null      = article page, no published counterpart in the other language
```

### `getPublishedCounterpartSlug` return shape

```ts
(translationGroupId: string, targetLanguage: Language) => Promise<string | null>
```

`null` means "no published counterpart" (covers both "no row exists for that group+language" and "a row exists but is unpublished") — the two cases are deliberately not distinguished by the caller, per the source spec's assumption that an unpublished counterpart is treated as absent.

## State transitions

None. This feature is read-only with respect to persisted data — it introduces no new write path, no new mutation, and no state machine. The only "transition" in play is the existing one (an article moving from unpublished to published via the admin CRUD, out of scope here), which this feature merely *reads* more correctly than before.
